How to Get a Good Guitar Tone

The tone in that background / song sounds like garbage. Sorry, just digital, and over-processed. Blues is especially subjective, but that was really poor. His suggestions are really vague, and it really is all about the recording.

Check this out:

https://youtu.be/t1VWYfOJ0Lo?t=863

This starts with the amps, but then goes to LIVE testing and monkeying around. Remember the sound is recorded not by the mix table, but the live mics they are using for the youtube video. Even with those crap mics it is awesome.

It actually becomes 'overprocessed' in the conversion from the WAV to the video output and then into YouTube. I struggle with this all the time with my videos because YouTube is well known for having a really bad audio quality. That being said, I'm open to people not liking my tone it is all personal preference. The point of the video was that I had a tone I liked, and was trying to help people find one they liked using the same methods that I use.

That said, I completely disagree. Tone starts with your guitar. Obviously a target amp is going to sound like crap, but once your past that you should be relying more on the guitar than amp for tone. It's not about finding the absolute perfect spot for your knobs on the amp, that just hones in on the tone your guitar is already making. If you have the guitar set up right, theres only so much you can do on the amp before you start sounding unnatural.

I respectfully disagree. Though I don't care for most of his music Jack White gets some quality tones out of garbage guitars. Billy Corgan used some old Sears brand (or other no-name) on Mayonaise, and whenever it wasn't being strummed it gave that feedback growl. Billy Gibbons uses whatever pretty guitar he feels like, and they dial the tone in to sound like every other guitar he has (see that rig-rundown).

I read a story about SRV recording Texas Flood ad there was a wall of about 30 amplifiers, all boutique, and vintage. That is where the sound came from. Amps, and playing style.

This is all subjective of course, and I'm speaking only of recording an actual cabinet with a microphone, no direct in.

Thats perfectly fair. Sorry this was a bit late in response, but I probably didn't give the amp as much credit as it diserved. That said, when you put a bunch of equal quality amps next to one another, its really the guitar that I think will make the difference. Like you said though, all opinion!

This is silly...as silly as having a 5 minute video explaining what the best colors are for painting a beautiful image. We can tread safer ground if we just say; tone is subjective, it should service the music you want to play, and it's most likely in your fingers. There is no such thing as 'good' tone, just like there is no such thing as a 'good' color. Stop chasing the dragon and focus on servicing the music.
